text:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-picker tweak I started seeing steady GPU memory growth on our perf worker. Not a sudden OOM, just an upwards drift across long runs. anyone else? :thinking:
ajay: saw a similar blip on canary. thought it was kv-cache churn at first. logs?
leo: paste logs? maybe workspace sizing got bumped up by the new heuristic.
maria: attaching small snippet from the run (nvprof-ish):
```
GPU total allocated: 12.8G -> 13.1G -> 13.3G -> 13.5G ...
Active allocations count: 1024 -> 1021 -> 1020 -> 1018
Free blocks count: 210 -> 209 -> 209 -> 209
```
maria: counts don't look like a classic leak (free blocks stable) but resident grows. feels like fragmentation or persistent pinned buffers.
sylvie: could be ephemeral CUDA streams holding onto temporary buffers until sync. did you see any stream warnings?
maria: none. nvprof shows repeated cudaMalloc/cudaFree pairs but nvtx traces show long-lived objects holding pointers through callback code.
ajay: did you run with --enable-prefetch? our prefetcher recently switched to retaining prefetched tensors in a thread-local pool to avoid reallocation.
maria: yep that's the suspect. repro script: `scripts/repro/prefetch-retention.sh` — it runs many short requests hitting kv-cache and prefetch path.
sheila: can you paste simplified repro command? I can run on a 16G dev box.
maria: `./repro/prefetch-retention.sh --model gptj --iters 10000 --batch 3 --prefetch=true --sync=1`
leo: quick experiment idea: flip the pool from "sticky" to LRU capped size 32 and see if resident stabilizes.
maria: tried cap 32 -> memory plateaued at ~12.9G, growth stopped. cap 0 (immediate free) -> stable ~12.6G. unbounded -> growth.
ajay: that points to buffer retention policy, not allocator bug. but why do free blocks count stay same while resident increases? fragmentation -> allocator may be handing back blocks but driver-level pinned allocations remain.
sylvie: also check host pinned buffers (cudaHostAlloc) — we had an accidental host-pinned path in prefetcher for async copies. those stay as pinned until freed.
maria: good catch — the prefetcher uses host staging pool for async copies. logging shows hostPinnedPool.size() steadily increases under load.
sheila: if host pinned pools grow, the OS may surface that as GPU resident. We should audit lifecycle: are we returning staging buffers to pool or leaking refs?
ajay: I instrumented object lifetimes: PrefetchEntry has shared_ptr to StagingBuffer, but our callback stores a raw pointer in a lambda capture for bookkeeping — that prevents shared_ptr from dropping.
leo: nasty. so it's a logical leak (dangling ownership) — buffers never freed even though application thinks they're returned.
maria: patch idea: change callback capture to weak_ptr and lock inside callback, or explicitly reset shared_ptr after async copy completes.
sylvie: also add telemetry: gauge hostPinnedPool.totalBytes and count, emit on console. makes debugging easier in future.
maria: created repro branch: `maria/prefetch-weak-capture`. quick diff:
```
- auto p = entry.staging.get();
- driver.async_copy(p, ... , [p](){ bookkeeping(p); });
+ auto wp = weak_ptr(entry.staging);
+ driver.async_copy(wp.lock().get(), ... , [wp](){ if (auto sp = wp.lock()) { bookkeeping(sp.get()); sp.reset(); } });
```
maria: running it now on canary. will update with profiler snapshot.
runtime-bot: CI job #8324 started: repro/prefetch-weak-capture (canary)
ajay: while that lands, consider allocator tuning: reduce min-block to 64k and enable coalescing on free path. reduces fragmentation risk for many small staging buffers.
sylvie: add a safety: after N prefetched entries leak threshold, trigger pool shrink (free oldest buffers back to driver).
sheila: ran the patched repro — nvprof snapshot shows resident stable across 10k iters. good sign.
maria: adding unit test in perf-tests to run the repro and assert resident delta < 200MB over 5k iters.
leo: nice. follow-up: file a postmortem note describing root cause = callback capture holding shared_ptr -> host-pinned pool growth -> apparent GPU resident drift. include mitigation: weak capture + pool cap + allocator coalesce.
ajay: also add a short-term rollout plan: canary -> prod-limited -> full, and a circuit breaker metric if hostPinnedPool.bytes > 1.5x baseline. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks team. I'll open PR and schedule a quick ops rollout today. tagging @sylvie @ajay for review.
